news.title: Portugal: Cristiano Ronaldo considered retiring from international duty after the 2026 World Cup.
news.lede: At 41 years old, Cristiano Ronaldo did not rule out turning the page on the Portuguese national team after the 2026 World Cup. After speaking with the president of the Federation and coach Jorge Jesus, the five-time Ballon d’Or winner ultimately chose to continue his international journey. Cristiano Ronaldo acknowledged that he seriously considered ending his international career after the 2026 World Cup. The captain of Portugal, who continues to perform at the highest level with Al-Nassr, changed his mind after discussions with the team’s management.

news.title: Bonus for the World Cup: Spain star gives up one million euros to federation employees
news.lede: A press report revealed today, Thursday, a stunning surprise concerning one of the players of the Spain national team, crowned champions of the 2026 World Cup. Money isn't always everything in football, according to newspaper "AS", and it pointed to a fresh example: someone who will wear two stars on his chest this Saturday at Wembley Stadium, where Spain face England in the UEFA Nations League. The player in question, whose identity the paper did not reveal, gave up his World Cup winning bonus and donated it to the staff of the Spanish Football Federation in appreciation of their outstanding efforts. news.title: India Set to Open International Football Window Against Panama
news.lede: New Delhi — The Indian men’s football team will open a major international window with a friendly against Panama at Sree Kanteerava Stadium in Bengaluru on Friday. The match will begin a challenging stretch for the Blue Tigers as they prepare to face several teams that competed at the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Panama, ranked 44th in the FIFA World Ranking, will be India’s first opponent before upcoming matches against Brazil and New Zealand. The Bengaluru fixture will mark the first meeting between India and Panama and only the ninth time India has faced a team from the CONCACAF region.

news.title: Panama Coach Offers Blueprint For India's Football Future
news.lede: Panama's national football coach, Thomas Christiansen, offers valuable insights on how India can emulate Panama's journey to becoming a notable football nation, emphasizing strategic development and global exposure. Panama's growth as a notable football nation came on the back of an intense jostling with baseball for space in public consciousness, eventually resulting in them appearing in two FIFA events in 2018 and 2026. Thomas Christiansen, Panama's longest-serving football coach since 2020, has seen that battle from close quarters, and thinks that India can take a cue from that. Christiansen understands that cricket is the No. 1 sport in India, but football can find relevance and space in the country with calculated steps.

news.title: Mayor Gaskins proposes Croatian friendship city after Alexandria hosts World Cup team
news.lede: Alexandria’s mayor wants to keep the connection going with Croatia after the city hosted the Croatian National Football Team as its World Cup home base. At Alexandria City Council’s meeting Tuesday (Sept. 22), Mayor Alyia Gaskins proposed a memo to establish a friendship city with Osijek, Croatia. Gaskins said the Croatian Embassy approached the city about ways to continue a partnership after the World Cup hosting.

news.title: Korea beat Ecuador 3-0 in Moreno's coaching debut
news.lede: Son Heung-min of Korea celebrates after scoring against Ecuador during their men's football friendly match at Suwon World Cup Stadium in Suwon, Gyeonggi Province, Thursday. Yonhap Korea blanked Ecuador 3-0 in their men's football friendly match at home Thursday, giving interim head coach Robert Moreno his first win in his debut with the Taegeuk Warriors. Oh Hyeon-gyu, Son Heung-min and Lee Dong-gyeong scored a goal apiece in the second half at Suwon World Cup Stadium in Suwon, just south of Seoul, in Korea's first match since the end of the FIFA World Cup in June. Korea suffered a group-stage exit from the tournament then, costing head coach Hong Myung-bo his job.

news.title: Infantino under pressure to include abandoned World Cup sell-off plan in external Fifa review
news.lede: Council members also want Balogun affair included. Fifa president says review letter been well received. Fifa council members will demand that Gianni Infantino include the abandoned World Cup sell-off plan and the Folarin Balogun affair in his proposed external review of Fifa’s governance. In a letter sent to all 211 of Fifa’s member associations on Monday, Infantino said he would ask the council to commission a review of “Fifa’s current governance framework for major strategic initiatives” at its next meeting, in Zurich on 15 October, but he faces an internal battle over its terms of reference.

news.title: ‘Utter Nonsense’—Virgil van Dijk Confronts Journalist Over Shocking World Cup Claim
news.lede: Liverpool center back Virgil van Dijk gleefully took the opportunity to challenge a Dutch journalist over what he felt were “completely baseless” claims about his performances at the World Cup.After the Netherlands’s disappointing round-of-32 exit at the hands of Morocco, Van Dijk was accused by Valentijn Driessen of “betraying” the national team by allegedly forcing a change in formation which did not pay off.Driessen, who had previously called the defender an “overblown narcissist” with a “dubious reputation,” was among the journalists present for Van Dijk’s press conference before facing Germany this week. Predictably, the Liverpool man was not in the mood for a friendly chat.“. It’s easy to say in hindsight: ‘We should have done this differently’ or ‘We should have done that differently,’” Van Dijk reflected.“.
